A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SBRT and surgery should not be considered mutually exclusive, as they each have advantages for different subgroups of patients.

SBRT is an effective treatment for early stage medically operatable lung cancer patients, but surgery should remain the gold standard for patients with larger, centrally located tumors with high risk of nodal metastasis.
SBRT and surgery are both effective treatment options for medically operable NSCLC, and that the best choice for treatment is highly dependent on the patient's individual characteristics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a subset of patients who would clearly benefit most from SBTR or surgery and that the debate is more nuanced than the generalization that SBRT should be used for all patients.
there is a subset of patients who will benefit most from either SBRT or surgery, and it is important for clinicians to consider patient‐specific factors when making this decision.
